title: ATP Yield Calculator: Work Out ATP per Glucose
description: Pick your P/O ratio and shuttle, see the full accounting per glucose, then check yourself with six questions on the parts students lose marks on.
intro: Six questions on the accounting above, each answerable from the convention and shuttle that produced the number.

questions.q: Using the modern P/O ratios and the malate-aspartate shuttle, what is the total ATP per glucose?
questions.why: Modern ratios of 2.5 and 1.5 with the full-value shuttle give 32, while the older 3 and 2 ratios are what produce 38.
questions.source: Worked example, modern accounting with the malate-aspartate shuttle: 4 + 20 + 3 + 5 = 32 ATP.

questions.q: The page counts 10 NADH per glucose. How many of them are made in the cytosol?
questions.why: Only glycolysis makes NADH outside the mitochondrion, so 2 are cytosolic and the other 8 come from pyruvate dehydrogenase and the cycle inside it.
questions.source: Stage table, Glycolysis row: 2 NADH marked (cytosolic); text says 2 of those 10 NADH are made in the cytosol during glycolysis.

questions.q: Why do those 2 cytosolic NADH change the total depending on the tissue?
options: Cytosolic NADH carries less energy than the mitochondrial kind
They are spent regenerating NAD+ before the chain can use them
NADH cannot cross the inner membrane, so a shuttle takes over
The cycle oxidizes them twice, once for each three-carbon half
questions.why: The NADH itself is identical, but it cannot cross the inner membrane, so the shuttle a tissue uses decides whether its electrons arrive worth a NADH or only a FADH2.
questions.source: Section How the total is actually built: NADH itself can't cross the inner mitochondrial membrane, so a shuttle moves the electrons across instead.

questions.q: With the classic P/O ratios of 3 and 2 and the glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle, what is the total?
questions.why: Classic ratios alone give 38, and the glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle then drops the 2 cytosolic NADH to FADH2 value, costing 2 ATP and leaving 36.

questions.q: How much ATP per glucose comes from substrate-level phosphorylation rather than the chain?
questions.why: Glycolysis contributes 2 and the cycle's GTP contributes 2, so 4 ATP are made directly and everything else comes from oxidative phosphorylation.
questions.source: Section How the total is actually built: every glucose makes 4 ATP directly, 2 from glycolysis and 2 from the TCA cycle's GTP; Total row, substrate-level 4.

questions.q: In a muscle cell on modern ratios, blocking glycolysis entirely costs how much of its 30 ATP?
questions.why: Glycolysis pays twice, 2 ATP directly plus 2 NADH worth 1.5 each through the glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle, so the loss is 5 rather than its own 2.
questions.source: Practice problem 2: total lost = 2 + 3 = 5 ATP out of 30, not just 2.
